advances: Ordinary Lebesgue retained caps in positive continuous dimension; the equality classification concerns retained caps.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The optimal caps, positive masses, centroids and almost-everywhere uniqueness of their optimizing indicators are supplied by efa4558174ce60cf, applicable at all the input marks and also at $y$ because the input interior balls combine into a ball in $K$.

Fix an orthonormal coordinate frame. Apply the conditional quantile construction in the proof of f6641f09c19819a3 to the full-dimensional $D_i$. Its maps $X_i$ send uniform cube probability to the uniform probabilities on $D_i$. Their positive own-coordinate derivatives $b_{ij}$ satisfy $\prod_{j=1}^d b_{ij}=|D_i|$. The same triangular substitution applies to $Z=\sum_i\lambda_i X_i$. Put $s=\sum_i\lambda_i s_i$ and $\omega_i=\lambda_i s_i/s$. The product $J$ of the own-coordinate derivatives of $Z$ satisfies
$$
\frac{J}{s^d}=\prod_j\sum_i\omega_i(b_{ij}/s_i)
 \ \ge\ \prod_j\prod_i(b_{ij}/s_i)^{\omega_i}=1.
$$
The inequality is weighted AM–GM for each $j$, with equality exactly when $b_{ij}/s_i$ is independent of $i$ for every $j$. By substitution, the density of $s^d$ times the law of $Z$ is $s^d/J(Z^{-1}(x))$ on its Borel image and zero elsewhere. It is feasible on $K$: it is at most one, has mass $s^d$, mean $y$, and is supported in the Minkowski combination of the $D_i$. This proves the bound.

If equality holds, uniqueness identifies that density with $\mathbf1_{D_K(y)}$ almost everywhere. Hence $s^d/J=1$ at almost every cube point, since the law of $Z$ is absolutely continuous and supported on $D_K(y)$ at equality. AM–GM gives the stated derivative equalities. This construction works in every orthonormal frame. In a frame with first axis a given unit vector $e$, the first coordinates $Q_i$ of $X_i$ depend only on the first cube variable and are the projected uniform quantiles. Thus $Q_i'/s_i=Q_1'/s_1$ almost everywhere by Fubini, and everywhere by their continuous derivatives. Integration and their means $e\cdot y_i$ give $(Q_i-e\cdot y_i)/s_i=(Q_1-e\cdot y_1)/s_1$. The upper quantile limits are the actual support endpoints, as projection densities are positive in the interior of each projection interval. Since this holds for every unit $e$, the bodies $(D_i-y_i)/s_i$ have identical support functions. Their common body $D_0$ has volume one and centroid zero.

The Minkowski combination is now $y+sD_0$. It is contained in $K$, has centroid $y$, and has volume $s^d$. Its indicator is optimal at equality, so uniqueness identifies it with $D_K(y)$ as a body. Conversely the stated cap identities give target retained mass $s^d$.
statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K_i\subset\mathbb R^d$ be finitely many convex bodies with interior marks $y_i$, and let $\lambda_i>0$ sum to one. Let the convex body $K$ contain $\sum_i\lambda_iK_i$ and set $y=\sum_i\lambda_i y_i$. For any such marked body $(H,b)$, let $T_H(b)$ be the maximum Lebesgue mass of a measurable density $0\le f\le1$ on $H$ with $\int_H(x-b)f(x)\,dx=0$, and let $D_H(b)$ be its unique optimizing convex cap. Write $D_i=D_{K_i}(y_i)$ and $s_i=|D_i|^{1/d}$. Then
$$
T_K(y)^{1/d}\ge\sum_i\lambda_i s_i.
$$
Equality holds exactly when there is a convex body $D_0$ of volume one and centroid zero such that $D_i=y_i+s_iD_0$ for every $i$ and
$$
D_K(y)=\sum_i\lambda_iD_i=y+\Big(\sum_i\lambda_i s_i\Big)D_0.
$$
title: Equality in joint physical retained-cap concavity
